name: Shavla Lakes
full: A chain of glacial lakes at the head of the Shavla river on the northern slope of the North Chuya Range (Lower, Middle/Upper and a nameless one at the source), 35–45 km on foot south of the village of Chibit (Chuysky Trakt, km 783). Above the lakes rise the peaks Mechta (Dream, ~3,600 m), Skazka (Fairy Tale, ~3,770 m) and Krasavitsa (Beauty, ~3,870 m).
near: Chibit village (35–45 km along the trail; km 783 of the Chuysky Trakt, fuel station); Aktash village ~5 km from Chibit along the highway
elev: Lower Lake 1,983 m; Upper Lake 2,164 m; nameless lake at the source 2,307 m (Bolshaya Strana); Oroy Pass ~2,045–2,290 m (sources differ: 2,045 / 2,220 / 2,229 / 2,290)
short: Turquoise glacial lakes under three snowy peaks — Mechta, Skazka and Krasavitsa; a classic 4–10-day hiking or horse route from Chibit via the Oroy Pass and the Eshtykel plateau, the “champion of beauty” in the words of Boris Delone.
desc: The Shavla Lakes lie at the head of the Shavla, a left tributary of the Argut, at the foot of the North Chuya Range. The Lower Lake (1,983 m) is the largest: about 1.5–1.7 km long and 370–500 m wide; the eastern shore is gentle, with larch forest and many campsites, the western one steep and rocky. The Upper Lake (2,164 m) is 610×110 m, up to 40 m deep, above the treeline, its shores strewn with boulders up to 5 m; higher up is a small lake at the source (2,307 m). Above the water rises a panorama of the peaks Mechta, Skazka and Krasavitsa with their glaciers; the mathematician and mountaineer Boris Delone called Lake Shavla the “champion of beauty”. The classic route is from Chibit: a vehicle drop to the Oroy Bridge, the climb to the Oroy Pass, the Eshtykel plateau (above 2,200 m), the descent into the Shavla valley; to the Lower Lake it is 35–45 km, 2–3 days, the whole round trip ~70 km (at least 5 days, comfortably 8–10). No phone coverage. An Altai family lives at the Lower Lake who run a banya (sauna), rent out horses, sell bread/groceries and offer guide services. Popular side trips go to the Upper Lake and to Mount Piramida (3,100–3,150 m). The place is very popular with tourists, and in summer there are many groups at the lake.
guide: Pitch camp on the eastern shore of the Lower Lake and get up at dawn — in calm weather Skazka, Mechta and Krasavitsa are reflected in the turquoise water, and the peaks are best seen in the morning. Do not rush on on the first day: once you reach the lake you can stay for a week (even guidebooks say so). Go light to the Upper Lake and, if you have the energy, up Piramida (about 3,100 m) — from there you can see the whole chain of lakes. Boris Delone, who travelled the Caucasus and the Alps, called this lake the “champion of beauty”. A banya at the local family’s place on the shore after three days on the trail is the best thing that can happen.
see: The Lower Shavla Lake with a view of Mechta, Skazka and Krasavitsa; the Upper Lake (up to 40 m deep) and the lake at the source; Mount Piramida (3,100–3,150 m) — a panorama; the Eshtykel plateau and the Oroy Pass; the “Idol Glade” with carved wooden figures at the Lower Lake (tonkosti); the glaciers of the North Chuya Range.
skip: you have fewer than 5 free days, no multi-day hiking experience and do not want to pay for a horse tour — without that you will not see the lakes. Also if you seek solitude in July–August: dozens of groups camp at the Lower Lake.
diff: Moderate (n/k, non-categorised): 35–45 km one way with ~900 m of gain on the first day (Chibit — Oroy Pass) and ~15 km of ascents, fords (Eshtykel 5–7 m wide, 0.3–0.5 m deep — skitalets 2020); days of 13–24 km; altitudes up to 2,300 m, a side trip up to 3,150 m. The horse option is easier, but part of the trail is impassable for horses (tonkosti).
when: From the second half of June to the end of August (sport-marafon); best from late July to mid-August (T—Zh); September is golden autumn, but with frosts and snow; July: ~+25 °C down below, ~+10 °C at 2,000 m.
hours: An open area; the hiking season is June–September.
daytime: Early morning — calm water and clear peaks; ascents — in the first half of the day (T—Zh); towards evening the rivers run higher from glacial melt (they rise during the day and drop by ~20 cm overnight — LiveJournal 2015).
how: Along the Chuysky Trakt to the village of Chibit (km 783; the bridge over the Chuya at Chibit is km 780.4). Then a vehicle drop to the Oroy Bridge (~1,500 ₽ per car — Bolshaya Strana), crossing the paid bridge (100–150 ₽ per person one way), the climb to the Oroy Pass, the Eshtykel plateau, the descent to the Shavla and up to the Lower Lake: 35–45 km, 2–3 days on foot. Buses to Chibit: from Gorno-Altaysk daily at 9:00 (the Kosh-Agach route), from Barnaul on even days at 8:40 (sport-marafon, 2024).
needcar: To Chibit — bus/car; beyond that — only on foot or by horse (or helicopter — mentioned by Altapress as an option, prices not found).
self: Yes, if you have hiking experience: the trail is beaten and popular, but you need to register with the Emergency Ministry (MChS), a track/map, a tent and a food supply; no phone coverage.
roadtype: Paved to Chibit; dirt road to the Oroy Bridge; then a mountain trail with fords and a boulder field (kurumnik) near the Upper Lake.
traveltime: Gorno-Altaysk → Chibit ~5.5–6.5 h (≈347 km — trekkingmania; by the highway km markers Biysk km 350 → Chibit km 783, i.e. ≈433 km from Biysk); Barnaul → Chibit 10–12 h; Chibit → Lower Lake 2–3 days (days of 13–20 km: skitalets — 13 km/+900 m on day 1, 20 km on day 2); Lower → Upper Lake side trip 8 km.
stay: Only tents at the campsites by the lakes (Bolshaya Strana). In Chibit before the start: bases Start from 2,200 ₽, Altai Kabai from 2,200 ₽, Altai Eko Kedr and Krasnye Vorota 7,000–7,761 ₽, Agory from 19,800 ₽ (mirturbaz 2026); the Kochevnik ECO tourist complex at km 781.5 (vtourisme). Parking a car at the base — 150 ₽/day, storing belongings 50 ₽/day (sport-marafon 2024).
net: No mobile coverage on the route and at the lakes — satellite only (Bolshaya Strana); in Chibit/Aktash there is coverage.
entry: Bridges: 100 ₽ per person for crossing (T—Zh, skitalets 2020, LiveJournal 2015) / 150 ₽ each way for each of the two bridges (Bolshaya Strana) — the total differs. Tour operators include “recreation fees”/“protected-area fees” (altaitg, zovgor) — the amount and recipient not found. The banya at the lake: 1,200 ₽ per group (2020), from 1,800 ₽ (Adventure Club 2027).
transfer: Chibit — Oroy Bridge ~1,500 ₽ per car; Gorno-Altaysk — Chibit transfer in tours +10,500 ₽ per person (Altai-Pokhod 2026); bus to Chibit — see above.
bring: Waterproof boots + spare shoes for fords, gaiters, trekking poles, a 70–90 l backpack, a sleeping bag with comfort down to −5 °C, two rain jackets/a shell, sun protection, a mug, cash (cards are not accepted), insurance with helicopter evacuation.
warn: Registering your group with the Emergency Ministry (MChS) is mandatory (T—Zh: 10 days in advance; MChS of the Altai Republic 8 388 23 9-99-99 per T—Zh — verify; online forms.mchs.gov.ru), check in before departure and after return. No phone coverage — evacuation only by helicopter, insurance is needed. Fords and rising water in the daytime; sudden rain and snow; rockfalls and boulder fields. Fishing: according to some data prohibited (Bolshaya Strana — “zakaznik”, a wildlife refuge), according to others grayling is caught (Altapress) — check. Ticks: as of 25.08.2026 the Altai Republic had 3,600 tick-bite reports and 22 cases of tick-borne encephalitis (Rospotrebnadzor) — get vaccinated/insured. Border zone: The border zone in the Kosh-Agach district covers only part of the territory: under FSB Order No. 282 (2006) — the Dzhazator, Mukhor-Tarkhata, Tobeler, Kazakh, Tashanta and Kokorya settlements; by FSB Order No. 512 of 13.10.2022 Mukhor-Tarkhata, Tobeler, Zhana-Aul and Kokorya were additionally removed from the zone (Tashanta, Belyashi and Argut remained in the zone). Kurai, Kyzyl-Tash, Chagan-Uzun, Aktash/Chibit (Ulagan district) are not on these lists — according to the data found, no permit is needed for this place (medium confidence: no official reply from the border directorate for this specific point was found). General rules: Russian citizens in the border zone need only a passport, a permit is required only for the 5-km strip along the border; foreigners need a permit for any point of the border zone (processing up to 60 days per the Sailyugem National Park site; 15/30 days per other sources). Where to apply: FSB border directorate for the Altai Republic, Gorno-Altaysk, 94 Kommunistichesky Ave., +7 388-22 4-82-00, pugornyjaltaj@mail.ru; branch in Kosh-Agach, 2 Armeyskaya St., +7 388-42 2-34-70. Keep your passport with you — document checks on the highway are possible.
food: Fresh bread and milk from herders/the family on the route (Bolshaya Strana: bread 70–80 ₽ in 2015, LiveJournal); grayling fish soup (Altapress — if fishing is allowed); in Chibit/Aktash — cafes by the highway.
reviews: No aggregator ratings for the place found; tours: Tripster (Andrey) — 4.82 (272 ratings, 233 reviews); “Alone with Nature” — 5.0 (2). Pros: “turquoise like the Maldives”, views of the peaks; cons: a hard route, rain, crowds in July–August.

p.sum: A multi-day route: Chibit (km 783) → vehicle drop to the Oroy Bridge (~1,500 ₽ per car) → Oroy Pass → Eshtykel plateau → Shavla → Lower Lake (35–45 km, 2–3 days). Tents, no phone coverage, a banya at the local family’s place. Registration with the Emergency Ministry (MChS) is mandatory. Horses 2,500 ₽/day + guide 3,500 ₽/day.
